Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

please adverb

classical

Plaut.
Ter.

amābō

With an imperative.

Other words

  • quaesō — please, I beg you

    first person of the old verb <span lang="la">quaesō</span>, thrown into the sentence; plural <span lang="la">quaesumus</span> · also used · classical · Ter. And. 204: Bona verba, quaesō.; Plaut. Most. 376

    The polite “please” of prose as well as comedy (Cicero’s letters: quaesō).

  • obsecrō — please, I implore you

    first person of <span lang="la">obsecrō</span>, often with <span lang="la">tē</span> · also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 765b: Manē, manē, obsecrō tē.

    Stronger than quaesō: “please, I beg you”. Plautus also spells it opsecrō.

  • sīs — please, would you (after an imperative)

    from <span lang="la">sī vīs</span>, “if you will” · also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 1: Exī ē culīnā sīs forās, mastīgia.

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

  • sōdēs — please, would you (after an imperative)

    from <span lang="la">sī audēs</span> (Cic. Or. 154) · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 103: Eāmus; dūc nōs, sōdēs.; Cic. Att. 7.3.11: jubē sōdēs nummōs cūrārī

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter., Hor.; Cic. in epistulīs)

Examples

  • «Id, amābō,» inquit, «adjuvā mē, tata!»

    “Help me with it, please, Dad!” he saidLibellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

  • Heus puer, dīc sōdēs…

    Hey, boy, tell me, would you…Ter. And. 84–85

  • Eāmus; dūc nōs, sōdēs.

    Let’s go; lead the way, please.Ter. Ph. 103

  • Exī ē culīnā sīs forās, mastīgia.

    Out of the kitchen, please, you rascal.Plaut. Most. 1

  • Manē, manē, obsecrō tē.

    Wait, wait, please.Plaut. Amph. 765b

  • Quaesō edepol, exsurge; pater advenit.

    Please, for goodness’ sake, get up; Father’s coming.Plaut. Most. 376

See also thank you, help, you’re welcome.
